Richard Stallman of the Free Software Foundation devised, in addition to some marvelous software, the GNU General Public License (GPL for short). Or the CopyLeft it is sometimes called.

It is quite a revolutionary document, using the "copyright" tool to to protect your right to use free software.

Unfortunately using copyright to protect free software is a lot like using a Jackal to guard the hens.

In fact, various inconveniences relating to this have resulted in modifications such as the LGPL (Library General Public License) and more recently the NPL (Netscape Public License)

I call these matters mere inconveniences, the real damage will occur when the Jackal's, (sorry, I mean lawyers), actually get to test the GPL in court for the first time.

Thus enter my version.

Its very simple.

Entirely consistent.

Completely unrestrictive.

Easy to apply.

The "No problem Bugroff" license is as follows...

The answer to any and every question relating to the copyright, patents, legal issues of Bugroff licensed software is....

Sure, No problem. Don't worry, be happy. Now bugger off.

All portions of this license are important..

    "Sure, no problem." Gives you complete freedom. I mean it. Utterly complete. A bit of a joke really. You have complete freedom anyway.

    Now bugger off. The only way to get rid of pushy Jackals is to ignore them and not feed them. The GPL is just begging somebody to take it to court. Can't you just see it. People got upset, started a fund, and hired, off all ruddy things, a Jackal to try and defend the chicken! Who really benefits from this trademark / patent / copyright thing anyway? The lawyers. OK so the last part of the license sounds a bit harsh, but seriously folks, if you are a :-

    Lawyer asking these legalese questions... You should go off and learn an honest trade that will actually contribute to life instead of draining it.
    Programmer asking these legalese questions... You have amazingly powerful tools in your hands and mind, use them to ask and answer the worthwhile questions of life, the universe and everything. Stop mucking about with such legal nonsense and get back to programming.
    User/reader asking these question... Don't worry. Go off and be happy. Have fun. Enjoy what has been created for you.

title: New license request: Hippocratic-3.0-core
body:
**1.** License name: Hippocratic License 3.0
**2.** Short identifier: `Hippocratic-3.0`, though `HL3` with suffixes seems to be the license author's preference (see below for more details)
**3.** License author or steward: Organization for Ethical Source
**4.** Comments: Note: this is a re-submission of https://github.com/spdx/license-list-XML/issues/1393, as suggested on the SPDX Slack. It almost entirely duplicates information from that issue.

### Has the license been approved by the OSI?

No

### Definitive factors

**Is the submitted license unique, that is, it does not match another license already on the License List as per the matching guidelines?**

Yes, it is unique - no matches running the SPDX tool. Also a substantial restructuring + new substance from the Hippocratic 2.1.

**If a software license, does it apply to source code and not only to executables?**

Yes - Section 1.4: “Software” means any copyrighted work, including but not limited to software code, authored by Licensor and made available under this License.

**Does the license have identifiable and stable text, and is not in the midst of drafting?**

Yes.

**Has the license steward, if any, committed to versioning new versions in the future and to not modify it after addition to the list?**

Unknown, but allegedly the Organization for Ethical Source were contacted back in early 2022 when [issue 1393](https://github.com/spdx/license-list-XML/issues/1393) was first raised.  There is no further mention in that issue of whether the OES responded, and if so what that response contained.

### Other factors for inclusion

**1. Does the license substantially comply with one of the free/open content definitions?**

No - the free/open definitions include variations of the theme such as that in the [Open Source Definition](https://opensource.org/osd) at 6 - The license must not restrict anyone from making use of the program in a specific field of endeavor. For example, it may not restrict the program from being used in a business, or from being used for genetic research. Hippocratic 3.0 contains many such restrictions.

**2. Does the license have substantial use such that it is likely to be encountered (ie. use in many projects, or in one significant project)?**

The definition of "substantial" as it is used here is unclear, but the [publisher of the license maintains a page that currently lists 29 adopters](https://firstdonoharm.dev/adopters/), and querying GitHub via the search APIs appears to show that at least 1000 repositories are using it.

Notes:

* This appears to have been the primary disqualifying criteria in previous requests for this license to be added to the SPDX license list. 
* The GitHub search UI _CANNOT_ be used to search for this license, since it isn't in GitHub's official list of licenses (it appears GitHub only supports SPDX listed licenses in their search UI - a chicken-and-egg problem when searching for as-yet-unlisted licenses such as this one).
* It is unknown if "at least 1000" means "1000" or "1000000000", as the GitHub APIs make querying more than 1000 repositories more difficult. A more sophisticated GitHub interrogation tool may be able to narrow down the precise number.
* The nature of those repositories is completely unknown - they may be forks, personal hobbies, empty repositories (apart from a license text), abandoned, etc. - again a more sophisticated GitHub interrogation tool may be able to estimate the "quality" of these repositories.

**3. Is the license structured to be generally usable by anyone, and not specific to one organisation or project?**

Yes - _use_ of this license is not specific to one organisation or project.  However as noted in [issue 1393](https://github.com/spdx/license-list-XML/issues/1393) software licensed _using_ this license has many field of use restrictions, so those _licensed works_ are not structured to be usable by anyone.

Notes:

* This appears to have been misunderstood or misstated in [issue 1393](https://github.com/spdx/license-list-XML/issues/1393).

**4. Is the license primarily intended to facilitate the free distribution of content with limited restrictions?**

No - the restrictions are not limited.

**5. Does the license steward support this submission, or is at least aware of and not in opposition of it?**

Unknown, but allegedly the Organization for Ethical Source were contacted back in early 2022 when [issue 1393](https://github.com/spdx/license-list-XML/issues/1393) was first raised.  There is no further mention in that issue of whether the OES responded, and if so what that response contained.

**Additional comments:**

The license publisher (OES) appears to prefer the identifier `HL3` for this new version of the license, with various suffixes indicating which module(s) are included (see below for more on "modules"). For example the license variant that includes all modules is referred to with the identifier `HL3-FULL` by OES.

Unlike its previous version (`Hippocratic-2.1`), the Hippocratic License 3.0 supports (at the time of writing) 16 optional "modules", each of which adds independent clauses to the core text of the license.  Any combination of the 16 modules is possible, resulting in a combinatorial explosion in the number of possible distinct license texts (typically each module adds one or more clauses to the core license text).

How this maps to SPDX constructs is an open question that needs to be answered, but this proposal does not attempt to do so as there are several ways that it could be done that leverage existing SPDX patterns. The license author (OES) appears to have adopted their own scheme based on suffixes (similar to how SPDX represents the `CC-BY` variants), but alternatively these modules may instead be expressible as new SPDX listed exceptions (in which case their definition should also be considered part of this request).

**5.** License request Url: https://tools.spdx.org/app/license_requests/496

title: Markup change to cryptsetup-OpenSSL-exception
body:
During license review in Fedora we discovered in https://gitlab.com/fedora/legal/fedora-license-data/-/issues/659 that
  sqlitestudio - https://github.com/pawelsalawa/sqlitestudio
uses this license:
  https://github.com/pawelsalawa/sqlitestudio/blob/master/LICENSE

That is GPL-3.0-or-later with an exception. The exception is very close cryptsetup-OpenSSL-exception it is missing at the end of first paragraph this part:

> ... under certain conditions as described in each individual source file, and distribute linked combinations including the two

Here is full text of the exception:

```
In addition, as a special exception, the copyright holders give
permission to link the code of portions of this program with the OpenSSL
library.
You must obey the GNU General Public License in all respects for all of
the code used other than OpenSSL. If you modify file(s) with this
exception, you may extend this exception to your version of the file(s),
but you are not obligated to do so. If you do not wish to do so, delete
this exception statement from your version. If you delete this exception
statement from all source files in the program, then also delete it here.   
```

I propose that we make this part optional so the reported license will match cryptsetup-OpenSSL-exception. An alternative is to add this as new exception.
